answer: The raven detector writes to glacier, and horizon shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 288 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 300 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 15 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
